## Summary

Set up a complete failover routing chain in the proxy where requests try Qwen3 locally first, then fall back to OpenCode Zen free tier (deepseek-v4-flash-free), then OpenCode Go (deepseek-v4-flash). Configure Pi to connect to this proxy and use the failover model.

## User Story

As a developer using the LLM proxy, I want to send a single request and have it automatically try local Qwen3 first. If no slots are available, fall back to a free remote model. If that is rate-limited, fall back to a paid remote model.

## Context

- The proxy config entry `qwen3-fallback` was partially added in `proxy/config.yaml` with three providers (local-qwen3, opencode-deepseek-free, opencode-go-deepseek)
- `proxy/proxy_remote.py` was modified to support the `model` field for upstream model name override
- A bug exists in `proxy/proxy/ui.py` where `_extract_router_model_ids` is called without being imported (NameError)
- Pi needs to be configured to connect to the proxy with the failover model as available

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `_extract_router_model_ids` NameError bug in `ui.py` is fixed
2. The proxy reloads successfully with the `qwen3-fallback` model entry
3. A request to `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: qwen3-fallback` returns a response (from whichever provider succeeds)
4. The response includes an `X-Provider` header identifying which provider served the request
5. Pi is configured to use the proxy with the failover model as one of its available models
6. All existing tests still pass
data.title: Complete failover plan configuration with Pi instance integration

# Epic: Implement proactive session compaction (two-tier)

Implementation umbrella for the approved compaction approach. Evaluation
evidence and recommendations come from LP-0MTAQNAQT002L746 (F1–F5,
`proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/*`) and LP-0MTAQNAIH001RN1S
(`docs/dev/hard-local-routing-cap-evaluation.md`); mode-specific
recommendations are in `docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md`
(LP-0MTC8BWV50012WSW).

Key evidence driving the split: 76.5% of estimated prefill work (2026-08-26)
was wasted on sessions whose context ratio exceeded 1.0 (can never be
resident in one slot → full re-prefill every turn); 99.1% of that waste is
concentrated in the top-15 sessions; decode collapse to <1 t/s observed.

## Sequencing (operator decision 2026-08-28)

**Client-side compaction first.** ContextHub has shipped compact-and-continue
machinery (WL-0MR269PDV00970YP, WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O) and is wiring the
gate-response handling (WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6). **Server-side (Tier 1)
implementation is delayed until results from the client-side effort are
reviewed.** Tier 1 is blocked on that review (see its item).

## Two complementary tiers

- **Tier 1 — proxy-side proactive compaction** (child LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD,
  DEFERRED/blocked): the proxy compacts the session at prompt-assembly time
  when estimated tokens exceed the trigger. Zero round-trip. **Strategy C
  (summarize-first) in both modes** (operator decision 2026-08-28): retain
  system prompt + very first user prompt verbatim + recent turns, fold the
  middle into a summary, truncate only as a logged backstop. Triggers:
  fast 58,300 (0.70 × 83,285) → target ≤ 38,000; cheap 43,000
  (0.70 × 61,440) → target ≤ 30,000, remote only when non-compactable.
  Enforcement gated on the quality experiment and client-side review.
- **Tier 2 — hard local-routing cap + cheap compaction gate** (child
  LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S): fast 70,000 / cheap 61,440 absolute caps; bypass
  local instantly above cap; cheap mode returns an informative gate response
  (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local prefill). Client-side
  counterpart in ContextHub (WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6).
- **Quality experiment** (child LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ): three-arm A/B/C
  validation that compacted-local quality is not worse than
  uncompacted-remote; gates Tier 1 enforcement.

## Goal

Ship both tiers with quality validated, cutting wasted prefill and
fallback pressure without silent content loss.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each child carries its own ACs. Epic closes only when all children are
  terminal and the quality experiment outcome is approved.
- No behavior change ships before its tier's gate is satisfied
  (Tier 1 enforcement gated on the experiment + client-side review; Tier 2
  is a routing-level safety net, operator-approved 2026-08-27).

## Dependencies

- Tier 1 depends on the quality experiment (design approval) and is blocked
  on client-side compaction results (ContextHub).
- Tier 1 and Tier 2 are complementary; Tier 2's hard cap is the final
  bypass guard that keeps compaction from ever being relied on alone.
data.title: Implement proactive session compaction (two-tier: proxy-side + hard-cap gate)

# Burst profile quantification (parent AC1)

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO
**Depends on:** T1 (log-based simulation harness singleton)

## Goal

Quantify the bursty fan-out profile of cheap-mode traffic from pre-2026-08-28 windows: concurrent local request distribution during bursts, observed queue depth, queue-wait duration distribution, and how many fallbacks occurred while the contention queue was non-empty.

## Deliverables

- A markdown report section (or committed analysis doc under `proxy/benchmarks/` / `docs/dev/`) presenting all quantified AC1 metrics for the replayed cheap-mode windows.
- Any reusable extraction code lives in the T1 harness; this item consumes it.

## Metrics (per parent AC1)

1. **Concurrent local requests during bursts:** distribution of `local_active_queries` (reconstructed from status_request/local_dispatch_denied active counts and stream lifetimes) during cheap-mode burst windows; burst definition from inter-arrival analysis (parent cites 95% of fallbacks within 60s of a prior fallback; median inter-arrival 4s, p90 21s).
2. **Queue depth observed:** distribution of `contention_queue_depth` from status_request snapshots and contention_queue_dispatch lines (which carry depth at dispatch).
3. **Queue-wait durations:** distribution of `queued_duration` from contention_queue_dispatch (dispatched) and contention_queue_fallback_after_queue (fell back, typically = wait cap).
4. **Fallbacks while queue non-empty:** count of `Fallback triggered` (cheap-mode, non-context reasons) that co-occur with queue_depth > 0 (via nearest status_request snapshot within a small time delta), where derivable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All four AC1 sub-criteria (concurrent distribution, queue depth, queue-wait durations, fallbacks-while-queue-non-empty) are quantified from the replayed pre-Aug-28 cheap-mode windows and presented in the report.
- Burst definition is stated explicitly (thresholds used, e.g. inter-arrival window / concurrency floor) and applied consistently.
- Methodology is documented and reproducible (script + command documented, following the conventions of prior benchmark reports).
- A comment is recorded on the parent work item LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO summarizing the burst-profile findings and citing the committed report path (if committed) or the raw script output path.
data.title: T2: Burst profile quantification

# Queue caps vs slots projected-gain analysis (parent AC2)

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO
**Depends on:** T1 (simulation harness), T2 (burst profile)

## Goal

Evaluate the expected gain of raising contention queue caps (wait/depth) vs raising slot counts in cheap mode: projected additional local dispatches saved per window, with the slots-vs-context trade-off factored in.

## Approach

- **Queue-cap scenarios (via T1 simulation):** sweep `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (e.g. 120s, 180s, 300s) and `contention_queue_max_depth` (e.g. 8, 12, 16) over the replayed cheap-mode windows; record projected additional queued→dispatched saved, residual fallback_after_queue, and added queue-wait latency percentiles.
- **Slots scenarios:** model 2→3 (and consider 2→4) slots in cheap mode.
- **Slots-vs-context trade-off (Q3 answer: A — reuse prior findings):** reuse the established trade-off from LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM / LP-0MSY0SDAS0031Y7F (more slots → smaller per-slot context → more `large_context_bypass`/`context_too_large` fallbacks). Do NOT run new benchmarks. **If reusing prior findings materially compromises the estimate, flag this prominently in the report** (notify-in-report requirement) and note the caveat in the recommendation.

## Deliverables

- Comparison table: for each scenario (queue-cap variants; slots variants), projected Δ local dispatches saved per cheap-mode window vs current config (2 slots, wait 60s, depth 4), with the context-bypass penalty stated.
- Explicit statement of which lever (queue caps or slots) has higher projected impact and why.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Queue-cap tuning projected gain quantified with concrete recommended candidate values (at least 2 wait values and 2 depth values evaluated).
- "Add slots" projected gain quantified with the context-bypass penalty included (per-slot ctx shrink → bypass increase), sourced from prior findings (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM / LP-0MSY0SDAS0031Y7F) with citations.
- Headline comparison produced: which lever recovers more local dispatch, with numbers.
- If prior benchmark findings were reused and materially affect the estimate, the report must state this caveat up front.
data.title: T3: Queue caps vs slots projected-gain analysis

# Recommendation + config change proposal (parent AC3/AC4)

**Parent:** LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO
**Depends on:** T1, T2, T3

## Goal

Record a concrete, quantified recommendation on this work item and create follow-up implementation item(s) if config changes are warranted.

## Deliverables

1. **Recommendation comment** on LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO covering:
   - Whether to tune `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` / `contention_queue_max_depth` (and to which values), per-mode if warranted (fast mode currently policy=fallback — no change there unless analysis supports otherwise).
   - Or whether adding slots in cheap mode is the better lever (with the slots-vs-context penalty).
   - Quantified expected impact (additional local dispatches saved per window) and risks (added queueing latency, user-visible stalls if wait cap raised, depth-cap clamp [1,16] limits, interplay with `llama_adaptive_timeout_*` budget subtraction for queued waits).
   - Data sources cited (T1/T2/T3 artifacts; prior LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM findings where reused).
   - Assumptions + unknowns recorded (OPEN QUESTION entries where appropriate; e.g. whether live validation is needed before rollout).
2. **Follow-up implementation item(s)** created via `wl create` when config changes are warranted, containing the concrete diff (config-cheap.yaml values) and rollout notes. Read-only task if the recommendation is no-change.
3. If the recommendation is a no-go for cheap mode but the analysis surfaced fast-mode or global opportunities, note them as discovered-from follow-ups.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Recommendation comment recorded on LP-0MTED3OFP006I7NO with concrete config values (or explicit no-change decision), quantified impact, and quantified risks.
- Follow-up implementation work item(s) created (via wl) if and only if config changes are warranted, with the concrete change and rollout plan; the item references this work item (discovered-from/related-to).
- Recommendation honors config clamps (wait ≤ session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds; depth ∈ [1,16]) and the fast-mode no-queue invariant.
- Any assumption that materially affects the recommendation is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION entry in the parent.
data.title: T4: Recommendation + config change proposal

# T2: Quantified prefill vs busy verdict and increment→first-byte distribution

Measure actual prefill time from llama-server eval-timing lines (total prefill seconds in window) vs decode/busy time (27.9% busy baseline), and — where derivable — the increment→Stream-started distribution; state which contributor dominates idle-time counts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Total prefill seconds in window are computed from llama-server eval-timing lines (or bounded estimate if logs rotated) and compared to decode/busy time (27.9% busy baseline).
- Distribution of time between `local_active_queries` increment (`proxy/proxy/server.py` + `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:_increment_local_active_queries`) and `Stream started` (first-byte at `proxy/proxy/router.py:1092`) is measured where derivable — median/p50/p90 reported, or "not derivable" recorded as unknown with bound estimate.
- Verdict states which contributor dominates the 290 idle-time `local_concurrency_limit` events: (a) prefill before first token, (b) contention-queue waits (`proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`, invariants LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D / LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I preserved), or (c) inactive lease/cooldown hold (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:_try_acquire_local_dispatch`), with numbers.
- Any helper analysis script is committed under `proxy/benchmarks/` or `scripts/` and covered by tests; no production routing change in this item.

## Tasks
- Parse eval-timing lines for the window; sum prefill seconds; cross-check against busy baseline.
- Trace `local_active_queries` lifecycle: increment at proxy request start → decrement at finish vs `Stream started` first-byte; derive distribution where correlation allows.
- Attribute idle-time fallbacks to (a)/(b)/(c) with counts; flag any lever touching queue/lease semantics.
- Commit helper script + tests if added.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `local_active_queries` / `local_active_queries_lock` lifecycle
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_increment/_decrement_local_active_queries`, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` lease/cooldown, adaptive lease helpers
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `stream_generator()` / `Stream started` at :1092
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_get_local_concurrency_info` (~1803) vs `session_slot_pool_size`
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — bounded cross-session contention queue (b vs c distinction)
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `session_slot_pool_size` single source of truth
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/fallbacks.csv` — CSVs and llama logs for the window (data source)

## Dependencies
- T1 (LP-0MTH4FVFA000QAOK)

## Deliverables
- Quantified verdict table + increment→first-byte stats (or bounded unknown) + dominant-contributor statement; helper script + tests if added.
data.title: T2: Quantified prefill vs busy verdict and increment→first-byte distribution

# T3: Hypothesis proof with time-aligned trace and 2–3 lever evaluations

Confirm or refute that `local_active_queries` over-counts busy with a time-aligned event trace, then evaluate 2–3 concrete levers to improve local processing time or reduce false-full reads with impacts quantified from window data.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Event-level evidence: a time-aligned trace (timestamps joined from proxy fallback CSVs + llama-server slot status) shows a burst of `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks during a llama-server idle stretch (0 active streams, no queued work) while `local_active_queries` reads full (≥ `session_slot_pool_size`=3) — confirming or refuting the over-count hypothesis (parent AC2); inconclusive correlation is recorded as unknown.
- 2–3 levers evaluated, each with expected impact quantified from the window data (estimated fallback reduction among the 290 idle events, TTFT/prefill delta, or busy-time reclaimed); levers justified from T2 verdict (e.g. count only generating toward pool, prefill/batching, adaptive lease, warm-cache/prompt-cache).
- Any lever that touches contention-queue or lease semantics is flagged w.r.t. LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D / LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I invariants and LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE (`session_slot_pool_size` single source of truth); `session_slot_pool_size` is not forked.
- No production routing change in this item; any helper scripts under `proxy/benchmarks/` or `scripts/` with tests.

## Tasks
- Join proxy fallback CSV timestamps with llama slot status + `local_active_queries` counter to build the trace.
- Model each lever against the 290 idle-time events; estimate fallback reduction / TTFT / busy reclaimed.
- Flag queue/lease-touching levers against their invariant work items.
- Keep `session_slot_pool_size` as sole pool-size source.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_get_local_concurrency_info` and `local_concurrency_limit` decision
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`, adaptive lease helpers
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — contention-queue invariants (LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D / LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I)
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `local_active_queries` / lock lifecycle
- `proxy/benchmarks/benchmark_harness.py` — harness for TTFT/prefill lever measurement
- `docs/llama-router.md` — routing docs (lever context)
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/fallbacks.csv` — window CSVs + llama logs (same sources as T1/T2)

## Dependencies
- T2 (LP-0MTH4FZ9G002NVK6)

## Deliverables
- Time-aligned trace artifact + hypothesis verdict + lever table with quantified impacts and invariant flags.
